title: If we confess (1 John 1:8–9)
hookLine: if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves

lines: THE BLUE DOT HAS TO BE RIGHT.
NO ROUTE FROM A PRETEND PLACE.
cards: A map app can get you almost anywhere, on one condition: it has to know where you actually are.
If the little blue dot thinks you're downtown when you're stuck on a country road, every direction it gives you will be wrong too, no matter how confident the voice sounds.
It can't route you home from a place you're pretending to be. A few lines into his first letter, John says something very like this about the soul. And he says it to believers, not to strangers.

teach.b: The Douay-Rheims: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." Notice the we. John doesn't point at outsiders; he includes himself, the one who touched the word of life.

The danger isn't sin so much as pretending, putting the blue dot somewhere it isn't. Then the turn: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all iniquity."

teach.h: HOMOLOGEO: TO SAY THE SAME THING.
teach.b: The Greek word for confess is homologeo, and some readers hear two pieces in it, same and say: to confess is to say the same thing, to agree with God about what actually happened.
Not to grovel, not to perform, just to stop arguing with the truth. Then John picks two surprising words for God.
Faithful, because God promised to forgive and keeps his promises. And just. You might expect justice to stand in the way of forgiveness.

John puts it on forgiveness's side. A few verses later he explains: we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ, who is the atonement for our sins. Catholics hear this passage in several places.
Near the start of Mass, in what's called the penitential act, the people confess together that they have sinned, before they hear the word.

teach.h: IF WE CONFESS OUR SINS, HE IS FAITHFUL.
teach.b: And in the sacrament of Penance, a person names their sins to a priest and hears the words of absolution. The Catechism quotes these very verses when it says that to receive God's mercy, we have to admit our faults.
Mercy can't reach a place you insist you aren't standing.

how: Catholics confess their sins together in the penitential act near the start of Mass, and individually in the sacrament of Penance, where a person names their sins to a priest and receives absolution; the Church asks Catholics to confess serious sins at least once a year.

o: to apologize until someone forgives you
to keep quiet and hope the sin is forgotten
to confess: to say the same thing as the truth

games.q: if we confess — tap the pairs.
p: God keeps his promise to forgive

s: John says faithful Christians no longer have any sin
he says if we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves. he includes himself.
John sets God's justice against forgiveness
he calls God faithful and just to forgive: justice is on forgiveness's side.
the Catechism quotes these verses on admitting our faults
to receive God's mercy, it says, we must admit our faults.

games.q: you did something wrong last week. nobody saw, and it's already fading. what does John say about telling yourself you have no sin?
o: it's fine if no one was hurt.
you deceive yourself, and the truth is not in you.
it only matters if it comes out.
games.why: John's warning is about pretending, not just about the sin. and the turn comes right after: if we confess, he is faithful and just to forgive.

practice: Look back over the past few days and let one thing surface on its own: something you said, something you didn't do, a way you treated someone.

Don't defend it and don't drown in it; say it plainly, in one sentence, the way it happened. If you pray, tell it to God and rest in John's line, he is faithful and just, to forgive; if not, let the plain naming be enough.

wordCard.voice: Homologeo, to confess. First John one: to say the same thing as the truth, and find God faithful and just to forgive. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: (if) we confess (1 John 1:9), often unpacked as homos, same, and legō, to say.

carryVoice: Your line: he is faithful to forgive. Faithful, and just. That's day six hundred fourteen.

sources.q: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all iniquity.
